subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — follow-up + quick ask on volumes

Hi Sophie / Ethan,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the candid run-through of BrightPay’s use case. Quick recap from our side and one small ask so we can put together an accurate pricing proposal:

Recap (from today’s discovery)
- Primary use: invoice parsing + contextual policy checks inside your customer portal (text generation for summaries + embeddings for search).
- Non-PII data flow into Redwood Hosted API (no private deployment right now).
- Current pilot: ~2k customers, planning to scale to ~20k over the next 12 months.

Open questions we need to price accurately
1) Expected monthly token volume (ballpark is fine — we just need to size tiers). Please include both generation tokens and embedding token estimates if possible.
2) Expected peak TPS (peak requests per second) — helps determine burst policies and whether a Dedicated SKU would be recommended.
3) Target unit economics: do you have a target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range we should aim for?

What we’ll deliver next
- A short 2–3 tier pricing proposal (hosted API) showing model choices and expected costs at your stated volumes.
- A recommended config (batching, cache, concurrency) to meet your latency SLOs while minimizing cost.

Attachments: I’ve attached the Redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf and an example MAAP estimate for similar customers.

Could you reply with approximate answers for 1–3 above by EOD tomorrow? That’ll let us prioritize the right model tier and sizing in the proposal.

Thanks —
Marissa

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — follow-up + quick ask on volumes

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — happy to confirm high-level numbers so you can draft the proposal. All numbers are estimates based on our product roadmap and expected customer growth.

1) Expected monthly token volume (generation + embeddings): ~200,000,000 tokens/month.
   - Rough split: ~160M generation tokens (summaries, short completions), ~40M embedding tokens (vectorizing docs + search).
2) Expected peak TPS: ~30 TPS (this is a conservative estimate for busy billing cycles — sustained baseline is closer to 6–8 TPS).
3) Budget / unit economics: we’re targeting a unit cost of around $35 / 1M tokens. That puts our target monthly spend in the range of $7k — $8k if volumes land at ~200M. If pricing is higher, headroom up to ~$12k/mo could be considered for 2026 Q2.

A couple of clarifying Qs:
- Do embedding tokens get billed differently on Redwood or do you count them the same way as generation tokens for your hosted plan?
- Are there any minimum committed spends for the hosted tiers at these volumes?

Happy to hop on a short follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Sophie Lane
VP Product, BrightPay
Sophie@brightpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — follow-up + quick ask on volumes

Hi Sophie — great, this is very helpful — thanks for the clear numbers. A few quick answers and next steps from our side:

Embeddings billing: For Hosted API we bill tokens consistently across generation and embeddings; however, embeddings usually have a lower per-1M effective compute because the model path differs. For the purposes of your target unit economics, treating them the same is fine for a conservative estimate — we’ll show a split in the pricing sheet.

Minimums / tiers: We have no mandatory long-term commit for the basic hosted tiers, but at volume levels where you’re trending 100–300M tokens/month we typically propose a reserved (discounted) tier or a small committed monthly minimum to get better unit pricing. I’ll include both pay-as-you-go hosted and a reserved commit example in the proposal.

Preliminary unit-econ check (very rough):
- Your target $35 / 1M tokens at 200M tokens -> $7,000/mo.
- At that price we can recommend: rtx-large-quantized variant for generation and a dedicated embedding-capable endpoint with caching enabled to keep latency low for search.
- If you need <50ms p95 for summaries, we’ll want to size concurrency and burst capacity — peak 30 TPS during billing cycles suggests we should plan a small burst buffer and routing policy to avoid throttling.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a 3-tier pricing proposal (PAYG, reserved-6mo, reserved-12mo) with modeled costs for your 200M token baseline and a 2x growth scenario.
2) If pricing looks good, short technical PoC (2–4 weeks) to validate peak TPS, p95 latency, and cache hit rates.
3) We can include estimated SLA/backstop terms if reserved commit is selected.

I’ve attached a draft proposal and a sample MAAP estimate for a comparable customer — see Redwood_proposal_BR P-042.docx and BrightPay_MAAP_estimate.xlsx.

Would you be available for a 20-min pricing review on Wed 3/3 or Thu 3/4?

Thanks —
Marissa

Folks — forwarding the customer reply with the numbers we need. Quick internal summary / ask: 

BrightPay qualifies as mid-market ARR motion with a likely initial spend target of $7k/mo (target unit-econ $35/1M tokens) at ~200M tokens/month. Peak TPS around 30 (baseline 6–8 TPS). They are open to reserved pricing if unit cost aligns.

Recommended next actions:
- Dylan: please draft a 3-tier pricing sheet (PAYG, Reserved-6mo, Reserved-12mo) that models 200M tokens and a 2x growth scenario. Include a row showing effective $/1M tokens at each tier.
- Logan: prep a PoC plan (2–4 weeks) that targets validating 30 TPS peak with p95 latency <100ms for generation and <50ms for embeddings. Include estimated infra needs and any test-data/ingest checklist for BrightPay.
- Marissa: I’ll schedule the 20-min pricing review for Wed 3/3 at 10am PT and own the customer comms.

Flagging: this is a good candidate for a small reserved commit to start (6mo) if we can get to $30–35 /1M effective with modest discounting.

Thanks —
Marissa
